newsitem.title: USA: U.S. medical equipment sales to Japan improving.
newsitem.headline: U.S. medical equipment sales to Japan improving.

text.p: U.S. trade officials Friday gave an upbeat assessment of a two-year-old agreement aimed at opening up Japan's $21 billion market for medical equipment.

A review this week of the 1994 agreement showed that U.S. firms in the past year enjoyed at least a 22 percent share of Japanese government purchases of sophisticated medical machines such as CAT scanners and other equipment, the officials said.

Japanese data show a much greater 38 percent share of their government medical equipment purchases going to U.S. firms, U.S. officials said. Because of the greater detail in the Japanese data gathered, Tokyo's figure is probably more accurate, but 22 percent is what Washington can verify, a Commerce Department official said.

The 1994 agreement, reached after bruising trade negotiations during which Washington threatened sanctions, covered government purchases. But U.S. officials said the benefit is spilling over to purchases by private medical facilities.
"When we talk to our companies, they are having success not only in the public sector, but also the private sector," said Deputy Assistant Secretary of Commerce Marjory Searing.

U.S. industry reports it is enjoying a 27 percent share of Japan's $21 billion medical equipment market. Before the agreement, the U.S. medical equipment industry reported a much lower 13 percent share of the Japanese market.
Searing said the Japanese market represents enormous potential for U.S. producers of sophisticated medical equipment.
"The market in general is a growing market," she said. "You've got an ageing population ... and their health care costs are going to rise substantially and their health care expenditures."
